subject: Production 429 spike — suspected project-tier assignment bug
messages:
From: Cory James <cory.james@medstream.com>
To: jonas_weber@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 28 May 2026 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Sudden 429s in production (api keys unchanged)

Hi Jonas —

We started seeing a large uptick in 429 responses this morning from the Redwood API for our primary project (medstream-prod). Error rate jumped from ~0.3% to ~12% between 02:00 and 03:30 PDT and has been noisy since. We haven't changed our client or retry policy.

Attached is a short tail of the Redwood responses and our client-side request IDs. We see a pattern where a subset of requests return 429 with x-retry-after headers, then our retries amplify the spike (retry storm). Our org-level dashboard shows project-level quotas were re-limited at 02:10 but we never triggered a usage commit.

Can you confirm whether anything changed on Redwood's side (quota reassignment, tier reclassification, or rate-cap policy)? This is affecting three critical workflows.

Attachments: redwood-logs-tailer-20260529.txt, medstream-quota-report-20260529.csv

Thanks —
Cory
Senior Platform Engineer, MedStream

From: jonas_weber@redwood.ai
To: diego_fernandez@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 28 May 2026 09:35:00 -07:00
Subject: FWD: Sudden 429s in production (api keys unchanged)

Team — Cory from MedStream reports an abrupt 429 spike impacting their production traffic. They included a small tail of logs and their per-project quota view. Key notes:
- Spike started ~02:00 PDT, sharp jump around 02:10 where their project-level quota appears to have been re-limited.
- They claim no client-side config change; retries are making it worse.
- Customer is high-touch; they are on a reserved capacity deal (DEAL-1429-MED).

Can Eng ops triage whether there was a tier assignment change, an automated rebalancer action, or a bug in quota propagation? Rishi, can you take lead on kernel/rate-limit config and include any quick mitigations (fallback to a compatible model variant, temporary burst lift)?

I will loop in Laura for executive awareness and Marissa for account comms.

-JW

From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
To: jonas_weber@redwood.ai, diego_fernandez@redwood.ai
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 28 May 2026 10:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: FWD: Sudden 429s in production (api keys unchanged)

Jumping in. Initial findings after a quick check of the quota service:
- At 02:09:42 PDT an automated job that reconciles org->project tier assignments ran and applied a stale mapping for MedStream. The mapping downgraded medstream-prod from their reserved tier to "standard-burst" due to a stale cache entry.
- The quota controller interpreted that as lower concurrency and applied tighter per-project rate limits.
- We have an open bug where the tier-reconciliation job does not validate last-updated timestamps before overwriting live assignments (INF-9876).

Immediate mitigation I recommend: 1) Roll the correct tier mapping back 2) Temporarily lift per-project limits for medstream-prod 3) Throttle retries via response hints / advisory header while we restore KV cache.

I'll prepare a rollback patch and a safe lift; ETA 45 minutes. Diego, can you confirm there are no related serving runtime regressions?

-Rishi

From: diego_fernandez@redwood.ai
To: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai, jonas_weber@redwood.ai
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 28 May 2026 10:28:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: FWD: Sudden 429s in production (api keys unchanged)

Checked serving runtime metrics — no kernel regressions, latency is normal for their usual model. The spike is purely quota gating leading to client retries piling up.

I've applied a temporary per-project limit lift and re-applied the reserved-tier mapping from the canonical store. Rolling back the reconciliation job's change fixed the immediate 429 rate; error rate dropped from ~12% to ~0.6% within 10 minutes.

I left a short runbook note with exact commands. We should follow up with a non-disruptive fix to the reconciliation job logic.

Attachments: runbook-rate-limits-v1.pdf

- Diego

Laura

Redwood Inference

From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: Cory James <cory.james@medstream.com>, Taylor Ng <taylor.ng@medstream.com>
Cc: jonas_weber@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Sat, 30 May 2026 18:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Sudden 429s in production (api keys unchanged) — mitigation and next steps

Hi Cory + Taylor —

Thanks again for flagging this and for the logs you sent. Summary of what happened and what we did:
- Root cause: an internal reconciliation job applied a stale tier mapping which temporarily downgraded your medstream-prod project, reducing per-project concurrency and causing 429s.
- Impact window: 02:09 to 02:21 PDT on 2026-05-28; peak 429 rate ~12%.
- Immediate remediation: we rolled back the mapping, temporarily lifted per-project limits, and suppressed advisory retry headers to reduce amplification. Error rates returned to baseline within ~10 minutes.

Next steps:
- Engineering will deliver a post-mortem and a fix for the reconciler job (INF-9876) within 3 business days.
- We'll add a safelist for reserved-tier projects and a validation pass in the reconcile flow.
- If you want, we can schedule a brief incident review with MedStream SREs and our Eng lead next week.

I've attached the short runbook we used and a CSV showing the quota delta during the window. Let me know if you want a calendar invite for the review.

Attachments: runbook-rate-limits-v1.pdf, medstream-quota-report-20260529.csv

Best —
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
